Senses.PreferredTarget: lose one's edge and be tongue-tied
AlternateTargets: have one's point blunted and tongue bound
be left without an edge or a word
Senses.Note: Six public-address cases document “lose one's edge and be tongue-tied” in four distinct works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒高步毘盧頂。不稟釋迦文。婢視聲聞。奴呼菩薩底來。也須亡鋒結舌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). English Label: Yuanwu Keqin says that even one who strides above Vairocana must lose edge and tongue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 平白地上拈起一絲毫頭，盡大地人亡鋒結舌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)). English Label: Mi'an Xianjie says that raising a single hair-tip on level ground leaves everyone without edge or speech.

Occurrences.Kwic: 道人行處萬境悄然一句全提亡鋒結舌且如何道得轉身句
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L158/L158n1652.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue Cong (明覺聰禪師語錄). English Label: Mingjue Cong brings the whole line forward and asks for a turning phrase after edge and tongue are lost.

Occurrences.Kwic: 虛空掛劍。殺活臨時。鞭起臨濟瞎驢。放出五祖鐵酸豏。盡大地人。亡鋒結舌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1999.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mi'an (密菴和尚語錄). English Label: Mi'an Xianjie says that when the sword hangs in space and the old exemplars are driven out, everyone loses edge and tongue.

Occurrences.Kwic: 平白地上。拈起一絲毫頭。盡大地人。亡鋒結舌。遠過恒沙國。近在口皮邊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1999.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mi'an (密菴和尚語錄). English Label: Mi'an Xianjie directly lifts a hair-tip on level ground and states that everyone loses edge and tongue, though it is as near as the lips.

Occurrences.Kwic: 設使三世諸佛歷代祖師出來。辯似懸河機如掣電。未免亡鋒結舌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). English Label: Yuanwu Keqin says that even if the buddhas and patriarchs came forth with river-like eloquence and lightning-swift function, they would not escape losing edge and tongue.

Senses.Explanation: Lose one's edge and be tongue-tied pairs loss of an edge with a bound tongue. Yuanwu applies it even to one who strides above Vairocana and again before raising a case; Mi'an applies it to everyone after a hair-tip is raised; and Mingjue follows it by asking for a turning phrase.

Senses.Explanation: The line says, “picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge, I casually see the southern mountain.” Yanxi Guangwen asks what is seen; Guxue Zhenzhe gives the line for the home-arrival sentence; Jieshi Zhipeng quotes Tao Yuanming; and Shuai'an Fanzong calls remaining there sitting in a grass nest.
